requirements.statement: Each additional content that appears when an interface component is hovered can be hovered by the mouse pointer without disappearing.

citations.quote: Chaque contenu additionnel qui apparait au survol d’un composant d’interface peut-il être survolé par le pointeur de la souris sans disparaître (hors cas particuliers) ?
Un composant d’interface est un élément avec lequel l’utilisateur peut interagir, par exemple un bouton, un lien, une zone de saisie.

routes.statement: The pointer can be moved onto the additional content without the content disappearing.

citations.quote: Pour chaque contenu additionnel, vérifier qu’il peut être survolé par le pointeur de la souris sans disparaître

exceptions.statement: Additional content controlled by the user agent, such as the tooltip of a title attribute or a native form-validation message.

citations.quote: Lorsque le contenu additionnel est contrôlé par l’agent utilisateur (par exemple, attribut `title` ou validation native de formulaire)
Des contenus additionnels contrôlés par l’agent utilisateur (par exemple, les infobulles associées à l’attribut title ou à la validation native d’un formulaire)

exceptions.statement: Additional content that becomes visible when the user activates something, such as a dialog window.

citations.quote: Des contenus additionnels devenant visibles par une activation de l’utilisateur (par exemple, une fenêtre de dialogue).

exceptions.statement: Additional content that is a modal window conforming to the WAI-ARIA dialog design pattern; the criterion is then not applicable.

citations.quote: ou correspond à une fenêtre modale conforme au motif de conception WAI-ARIA `dialog`, le critère 10.13 est non applicable.

rationale.text: The test has one requirement with one route: content that appears when an interface component is hovered can itself be hovered without disappearing. The exceptions are content controlled by the user agent (title tooltips, native validation messages), content that appears on an activation (a dialog), and a modal window conforming to the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern. Particular case 2 concerns test 10.13.1 only. The candidate is none. The custom check hovers each interface component it can identify, records text that appears, hovers one free point of the nearest wrapper that is not a component to rule out the wrapper, and then moves the pointer from the component onto one point of the text. Its fault is evidence only, because it does not establish two premises of a failure. First, comparing one point on the component with one point on the wrapper does not prove that the component shows the content. The reveal can depend on which part of the wrapper is hovered, and CSS can reach elements other than the hovered element and its ancestors. In Codex's browser fixture, the rule `#wrap:hover:not(:has(#dead:hover)) + #extra` shows an adjacent paragraph when the button inside the wrapper is hovered, hides it at the free point the check picks (a plain region of the wrapper), and still shows it at another point of the wrapper even with the button removed. The button is not needed, and the wrapper is not an interface component in the check's inventory, so the witness may not be content that appears on hover of an interface component at all. A script that reads the pointer position or the event target can do the same. Second, one point on the content does not rule out every way the pointer could reach it: a panel can close when the pointer enters a dismiss area over the chosen character while the rest of the panel stays hoverable, and a script can remember earlier runs. So a fault does not prove that the content cannot be hovered. The link keeps its routes and its partial scope and becomes evidence_only. What would raise the entry: a check that proves the identified component causes the reveal (not the wrapper's hover, a sibling or :has selector, or a pointer-dependent script) and that the content cannot be hovered through any viable region or path, with comparable starting states between runs, and fixtures for the wrapper case above, a component-triggered unreachable case and a reachable alternative-path control. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: whether a page has any content that appears on hover is only known by hovering everything in every state. Needs is state: the content the test is about appears only after an interaction, hovering.

citations.quote: peut-il être survolé par le pointeur de la souris sans disparaître
Retrouver dans le document les contenus additionnels devenant visible au survol d’un composant d’interface
Lorsque le contenu additionnel ne masque ou ne remplace aucun contenu porteur d’information, le test 10.13.1 est non applicable.
